purpose: Neutral grayscale atlas tinted by authored palette colors. Only material appearance changes; camera and environment stay at baseline.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production game material ALBEDO ATLAS, one square 2048x2048 raster image divided into an EXACT 4 by 4 equal grid. Sixteen contiguous square UV cells, absolutely no gutters, frames, captions, text, labels or margins.
Primary request: author detailed hand-painted game textures for rebuilding the supplied woodland village image as actual 3D models. The reference is STYLE ONLY. Do not draw the village or any building perspective. This is a flat, orthographic, evenly illuminated material texture atlas.
Critical format: all cells must be NEUTRAL GRAYSCALE to be tinted with the existing vertex colors in Godot. Keep most pixels pale gray between 65% and 95% brightness, a few dark structural marks around 40%. Material color comes from the model, not this atlas. No colored tiles, no baked cast shadows, no 3D render, no ambient occlusion vignette around cell borders.
Precisely ordered cells, read left to right, top to bottom:
Row 1: (1) aged lime plaster, large soft irregular plaster trowel planes and a few hairline cracks; (2) weathered oak timber running vertically, clear winding grain, occasional knots, broad hand-painted grain bands; (3) smoother cut oak for window frames, subtle vertical grain and worn edges, no drawn framing hardware; (4) ONE individual weathered clay roof shingle filling the square, broad uneven clay surface with chipped lower corners and mineral wear, not an entire roof and not a grid of tiny shingles.
Row 2: (5) irregular old stone wall masonry, five to seven large stones with thin recessed mortar and subtle moss flecks, not dozens of tiny bricks; (6) deeply furrowed old oak BARK, vertically meandering long grooves, branching fissures, broad gray ridges and a few lichen patches; (7) compacted village earth with broad quiet soil variations and sparse little gravel marks; (8) irregular flat limestone paving, several broad angular worn stones with shallow narrow joints.
Row 3: (9) ONE broad oval oak leaf viewed flat, base at bottom and tip at top, full-width midsection, visible branching central vein, shallow serrations and a few broad mottled patches; (10) ONE smaller obovate shrub leaf, tip up, base down, a clear central midrib and graceful secondary veins; (11) ONE elongated lanceolate leaf, top tip and bottom stem, distinct fine central vein and paired branch veins; (12) ONE pale five-petaled woodland flower viewed face-on, shallow petal vein texture, dark small center.
Row 4: (13) soft moss and lichen islands designed as broad interlocking organic patches, restrained detail; (14) old vertical wooden door planks with subtle seams, beautiful long grain and small worn chips, no handles or hinges; (15) quiet old window glass, near-uniform light gray with very subtle broad waviness and streaks, no reflections of a scene; (16) ONE pale weathered cut foundation stone filling the square, worn chipped edges and broad mineral changes.
Leaf cells: backgrounds pale gray, leaf body medium-light gray, veins lighter and darker gray; no black backgrounds. Existing modeled leaf geometry will define silhouette.
Style: carefully authored HIGH DETAIL stylized hand-painted game textures. Match the reference's intentional color grouping through broad material marks, with finer meaningful grain, veins and cracks visible up close. Crisp purposeful texture edges and a few subtle stepped contours. Refined readable detail, never photographic noise, glitter or dense random speckles. Maintain strong structural texture readability at 512 pixels per cell. Consistent neutral frontal lighting across every cell. Non-leaf material cells tile naturally within their boundaries.
Constraints: exact equal 4x4 grid aligned to 25%,50%,75% positions, no visible grid lines, no titles, no color swatches, no render of objects, no perspective, no lighting modifications.
